newsitem.title: JAPAN: US TREASURIES STILL LIMPING IN TOKYO AFTER NY FALL.
newsitem.headline: US TREASURIES STILL LIMPING IN TOKYO AFTER NY FALL.

text.p: Cash and futures U.S. Treasuries extended losses by Tokyo midday on Friday on follow-through selling and profit-taking from late overnight in New York.

"This morning we've got a good flow of sellers in the market," a trader at a U.S. brokerage firm said. "With the T-bond breaking a technical support, the market is looking for an appropriate level to enter new short positions."
Traders said sentiment turned even weaker after prices quickly dropped after the 30-year bond auction overnight and such a mood was persisting in Tokyo on Friday morning.
The new benchmark 6-3/8 percent 30-year bond stood at 98-4/32, yielding 6.52 percent, compared with 98-5/32 in New York on Thursday.
Traders said the market was still hurting from the recent jump in yields after the release of stronger-than-expected U.S. jobs data last week.

"The sentiment turned even weaker after yields broke above 6.5 percent overnight," a Japanese bank trader said. "There could be some bargain-hunting demand, but at this point, it's very difficult to determine where would be the right buying level."
The Japanese trader said the market should receive further direction from a slew of U.S. inflation-related data next week, including U.S. retail sales and the producer price index.
"Whether the yield (of the 30-year bond) falls back from this level or climbs above 6.6 percent will depend on the indicators," he said. "Until then, trading should be cautious."
Even greater declnes were seen this morning in the futures market, where operators were eager to test the downside, but the key September futures contract seemed to find firm support around 114.
The September T-bond futures contract stood at 114 at midday, down 7/32 from the previous close. It moved in a range of 114-00/32 to 114-12/32.

"There is potential for more losses in this market in the short term. For the time being, the market seems to have found support in Asia, but selling pressure may grow in the European market," the U.S. brokerage trader said.
"We currently see support in the 114-00 to 114-01 area, but below that (September T-bonds) could easily dip to 113-12/32," he added.
